response.sql: SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.bats), ''), 'Unknown') AS bats, COUNT(*) AS winners, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON p.player_id = ma.player_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.bats), ''), 'Unknown')

assumptions.assumption: Each manager_award row (one award won by a person in a given year) counts as one winner, so a person who won several times is counted several times. The request's wording 'use only awards that match a record in player' points to counting awards.
NULL, empty and whitespace-only bats values are merged into a single group labelled 'Unknown'.
Inner join to player drops awards with no matching player; player_id is assumed unique in player. The share is the exact, unrounded fraction of the matched total.

alternatives.interpretation: Count distinct people who won a manager award, rather than award records. Shares are of the distinct-winner total.
alternatives.sql: SELECT COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.bats), ''), 'Unknown') AS bats, COUNT(DISTINCT ma.player_id) AS winners, COUNT(DISTINCT ma.player_id) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT ma.player_id)) OVER () AS share FROM manager_award ma JOIN player p ON p.player_id = ma.player_id GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(p.bats), ''), 'Unknown')
